research_rationale: Read the whole order (18 FR 2069, signed 1953-04-10; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10444.txt). The restated text establishes the Good Conduct Medal for exemplary behavior, efficiency and fidelity, under regulations the Secretary of the Army and the Secretary of the Air Force prescribe, for enlisted men of the Army and Air Force who on or after August 27, 1940 completed three years of active Federal military service, or who after December 7, 1941 served one year of active Federal military service while the United States is at war, or who at termination of service had completed less than three years if any part was after June 27, 1950, with a proviso that no one, except persons separated by reason of physical disability incurred in line of duty, receives the medal for service of less than one year. The order has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes. later-events:ofr_catalog has 1 hit, the Office of the Federal Register note that this order amends EO 8809 (with a see-reference to EO 9323); that is the order's own effect on its parent, not a later event against it. current-law:usc has 1 hit, the note at 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57 that prints Ex. Ord. No. 8809 as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 9323, Ex. Ord. No. 10444 (Apr. 10, 1953, 18 F.R. 2069) and Ex. Ord. No. 14085, sec. 2 (Oct. 3, 2022, 87 F.R. 60541), with no ending statement. current-law:ecfr has 0 hits. A search of the held texts for the number 10444 finds the order's own copies, Executive Order 14085, Executive Order 10445 (which makes conforming editorial notes in the Army and Air Force regulations in 32 CFR parts 578 and 878 and does not amend this order), the 1989 Office of the Federal Register codification of EO 8809 (which records that EO 8809 was amended and restated by this order), and Federal Register pages of 1954 and 1967 whose authority citations name this order; none revokes or supersedes it. research_rationale: Executive Order 12109 of December 28, 1978 (44 FR 1067; held official text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12109.txt, read in full) has two numbered sections. Section 1-101 designates the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, to exercise the President's authority under 5 U.S.C. 5948 to prescribe regulations, criteria and conditions for payment of comparability allowances to recruit and retain certain Federal physicians. Section 1-102 provides that, until the Office of Personnel Management is established (on or before January 1, 1979) under Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978, the Civil Service Commission exercises that authority. The packet inventory already separates the two sections, so no inventory correction was needed. Section 1-102 ended by its own terms when the Office of Personnel Management was established: the held text of Executive Order 12107 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12107.txt), section 1-101, provides that the establishment of the Office of Personnel Management under sections 101 and 103 of Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978 is effective on January 1, 1979. Executive Order 12107 does not amend Executive Order 12109 and is cited only for that date. Section 1-101 has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes. current-law:usc has 1 hit, the U.S. Code note that prints this order under 5 U.S.C. 5948, with no ending statement. current-law:ecfr has 1 hit, 5 CFR part 595 (Physicians' Comparability Allowances), whose authority line cites E.O. 12109, 44 FR 1067, Jan. 3, 1979 (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/cfr-t5-part595.txt). later-events:ofr_catalog has 0 hits and the Office of the Federal Register catalog record carries no disposition note. A search of the held texts for the number 12109 finds only the order's own copies, the 1989 Office of the Federal Register codification (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_12109.txt, which records no later instrument) and 5 CFR part 595; none amends, revokes or supersedes the order. The authority statute 5 U.S.C. 5948 (held text jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s5948.txt) is in force: its 2000 amendments (Pub. L. 106-571, section 2(a)(1)) struck the earlier sentence that barred agreements after a fixed date, and subsection (a) still refers to regulations that the President or his designee may prescribe. The U.S. Code edition searched is release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected in it.
savings_reason: Section 1-102 ended on January 1, 1979 when the Office of Personnel Management was established; it was a transitional allocation of the same delegated authority to the Civil Service Commission, and no action under it needs saving beyond what the continuing delegation in 1-101 and 5 CFR part 595 already govern. No claim is made that any residual duty under 1-102 survives.
earlier_end_check: Section 1-101 has no end date, event or condition, and no held instrument ends or amends it. Section 1-102 ends by its own terms when the Office of Personnel Management is established; the held text of Executive Order 12107 section 1-101 dates that establishment to January 1, 1979, which is also the latest date section 1-102 itself allows. No earlier establishment date appears in the held texts.
scope_check: The packet inventory has two clauses, 1-101 (characters 811-1247) and 1-102 (characters 1248-1550 of the held text), which together cover every operative sentence from the authority recital through section 1-102; no command lies outside them.
independent_command_check: The designation of the Director of the Office of Personnel Management in 1-101 is independent of the Civil Service Commission's transitional exercise in 1-102: 1-102 ended on its own terms on January 1, 1979 while 1-101 continues, so each is tracked separately.
savings_check: The only ended command is the transitional exercise by the Civil Service Commission, which no longer exercises the authority; 5 U.S.C. 5948 and 5 CFR part 595 continue under the 1-101 delegation, so no residual under 1-102 is claimed.
